title: review: H5b fix round 1: the review re-spawn guard skips only tasks already stamped respawned_at for the current requeue, not any task with leftover pipeline keys; the five acceptance tests at 3164bed stay green (review T-0391)
spec:
STEP 0: the worktree must contain ec54196 and 3164bed (T-0363, H5b code and its five acceptance tests) in git log; never drop or amend them. Review T-0391 judged ec54196 before 3164bed added the tests; its first finding is answered by 3164bed (confirm the five tests exist and pass, do not rewrite them). Remaining finding:
1. (med) orchestrator/daemon.py:561 the guard `if pipeline or pipeline.get("respawned_at"): continue` is equivalent to `if pipeline: continue`, so any queued review or spec_review carrying an unrelated leftover pipeline key (a stale spec_review_error or dispatch_error stamp) is never re-spawned, defeating the once-per-requeue stamp. Fix: skip only when pipeline.respawned_at is present and later than the task's most recent "process died; requeued" event (or than claimed_at when no such event exists); a task with other pipeline keys but no current respawned_at is re-spawned once. Test: tests/test_daemon.py::test_respawn_ignores_unrelated_pipeline_keys (a queued review with pipeline {spec_review_error: ...} and a requeue event is re-spawned and stamped; a second tick does not re-spawn it; a later requeue event makes it eligible again).
Keep the five T-0363 tests and every existing test green. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh from the worktree root until it exits 0, then git add -A and git commit with the task id; report sha and failures only.
acceptance: git log --oneline in the worktree shows 3164bed and ec54196 below your commit
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree

comments.issue: bus.events(limit=10000, task_ids=[task["id"]]) is a global cursor query (`where seq>0 order by seq limit 10000`), not a per-task lookup. It returns only the oldest 10000 events ever recorded system-wide. Once the bus's lifetime event count passes 10000 (routine for a long-running daemon), any queued review/spec_review task created afterward has zero matching rows here, so `created_at` falls back to `default=now`, `now - created_at` is always 0, and `not died and now - created_at < respawn_after` is always True — the 'unclaimed task, spawn thread vanished before bus.claim' recovery path silently stops firing forever for newer tasks. The died-worker path is unaffected since it short-circuits before this check, but the delay-based path (covered by test_dispatch_respawns_unclaimed_spec_review_after_delay) degrades exactly when the system has been running long enough to need it. Tests pass because sandboxes never approach 10000 events. Use the task's own data (e.g. track created_at on the task, or query events ordered by seq desc / since a recent cursor) instead of an unscoped global-log scan.

_requeue now does two separate bus.locked()/bus.update() round trips for one logical reset (clear_stage's update, then a second update to pop respawned_at), appending two events to the task's history for a single requeue. Not incorrect (respawned_at is still cleared before dispatch() re-reads it), but the extra read-modify-write could be folded into clear_stage's existing pipeline_fields update to avoid doubling event volume, which matters given the global-event-log scaling issue above.
